definition: Every relatum has finitely many distinct upstream ancestors reachable by a nonempty finite path in the supplied causal relation; no modal or temporal bound is asserted.
note: Unattributed analyst vocabulary for #367, not a reading of Pruss or Koons. Uses Mathlib Set.Finite on {y | Relation.TransGen cause y x}; includes indirect ancestors and counts distinct relata, allowing repeated visits unless loops are separately excluded. Source scope and remaining gaps: docs/notes/causal-finitism-367.md.
